discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 091043
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
643 AM EDT Fri Oct 9 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- A few sprinkles are possible toward Lake Michigan today.

- More widespread light rain is expected Saturday night into early
  Sunday, especially east of I-69, associated with the remnants
  of Isaias. No significant impacts are anticipated.

- Generally above normal temperatures expected through much of
  next week before a more pronounced drop in temps is expected
  later Friday into the weekend. 
  

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 238 AM EDT Fri Oct 9 2026

Dry airmass in place across the region with a warm front well 
to the southwest from SE Nebraska to SW Missouri. This front is 
currently aiding scattered showers and storms across portions of
Iowa. While the front will make slow progress NE over the next 
24 hours, the area of precip will try to work NE well ahead of 
it, but run into increasingly dry air with some saturation 
starting in the mid levels. Given the dry airmass, suspect more 
of a sprinkle vs light rain risk, but for now have just lowered 
pops to slgt chc category. 

Focus then shifts to warmer temperatures on Saturday and
eventually some impacts from what will be left of Hurricane
Isaias late in the weekend. Highs will climb into the 70s and
maybe a few 80s in far SW areas on Saturday prior to the arrival
of a spoke of energy and inverted trough that pushes north
Saturday night into early Sunday. The main sfc and upper level
remnants will track along the Ohio River, reaching West Virginia
by 6Z/12. An area of generally light rainfall will impact the 
southeast third to maybe half of the area. Bit higher rainfall
amounts are likely in far SE sections (SE of I-69) where some
locations could see up to a half inch. Wind gusts will pick up
somewhat as well in this window in the same areas. 

Upper level ridging will try to take hold into mid week, but a 
weak northern stream trough will drop in for Monday night into 
Tuesday with another brief warmup Monday (maybe more locations 
touching 80). Mid to late week will then feature likely phasing 
of northern and southern stream systems, carving out a deeper 
trough with the sfc reflection remaining well NW of the area. A 
strong cold front looks to bring a much more fall like air mass 
in its wake just outside the current period with 850 mb temps 
dropping below 0 C.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z TAFS THROUGH 12Z SATURDAY/...
Issued at 642 AM EDT Fri Oct 9 2026

VFR conditions are expected at the terminals, with calm/variable
winds strengthening out of the S-SE through the period. A few
sprinkles are possible at KSBN this afternoon/evening, but no
impacts are expected. Left out of TAF for now given low
confidence-there is a lot of dry air to overcome. Otherwise, 
expect mid-high level clouds and dry conditions. 

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Fisher
AVIATION...MCD

spc.summary: With the approach of Hurricane Isaias, tornado potential will steadily increase this afternoon and continue tonight, especially across the Florida Panhandle into southeast Alabama and southwest Georgia.
spc.text:
SPC AC 091613

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1113 AM CDT Fri Oct 09 2026

   Valid 091630Z - 101200Z

   ...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS THE FLORIDA
   PANHANDLE INTO NORTHERN FLORIDA...SOUTHEAST ALABAMA...AND SOUTHWEST
   GEORGIA...

   ...SUMMARY...
   With the approach of Hurricane Isaias, tornado potential will
   steadily increase this afternoon and continue tonight, especially
   across the Florida Panhandle into southeast Alabama and southwest
   Georgia.

   ...Florida Panhandle into northern Florida/southern Alabama/southern
   Georgia...
   Reference the National Hurricane Center for the latest forecast
   track/intensity details regarding Hurricane Isaias. The latest
   discussion indicates that Isaias has reached major hurricane status
   as it moves north-northeastward toward the western Florida
   Panhandle/far southern Alabama.

   As Isaias approaches the coast, rainbands on its eastern periphery
   will spread northward toward the Big Bend of the Florida Panhandle,
   far southeastern Alabama and southwestern Georgia this afternoon
   into tonight. Throughout the day, a more unstable airmass over the
   eastern Gulf will advance northward, resulting in destabilization
   over the coastal areas of the Florida Panhandle. The current VAD
   profile at KTLH is already supportive of tornado potential (i.e.,
   0-1 SRH over 250 m2/s2), and low-level winds and SRH will strengthen
   significantly this afternoon and evening. Once the mid 70s F
   dewpoints come onshore, persistent, deeper updrafts will be possible
   with the propensity to rotate and have the potential to produce
   tornadoes, particularly across the Florida Panhandle into
   southeastern Alabama and southwestern Georgia.

   Additionally, some enhancement to the wind field, potentially
   including a convective influence, may occur across southern Alabama
   in vicinity of the evolving inverted surface trough late this
   afternoon into tonight.

   ..Jirak/Smith.. 10/09/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 2000Z

spc.summary: The threat for a few tornadoes will exist from the Florida Panhandle into parts of Georgia and the Carolinas Saturday through Saturday night. Isolated severe storms capable of severe wind gusts and perhaps a tornado appear possible over the lower Colorado Valley Saturday afternoon through Saturday night.
spc.text:
SPC AC 090550

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1250 AM CDT Fri Oct 09 2026

   Valid 101200Z - 111200Z

   ...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FROM THE NORTHEAST
   GULF COAST INTO THE SAVANNAH RIVER VALLEY...

   ...SUMMARY...
   The threat for a few tornadoes will exist from the Florida Panhandle
   into parts of Georgia and the Carolinas Saturday through Saturday
   night. Isolated severe storms capable of severe wind gusts and
   perhaps a tornado appear possible over the lower Colorado Valley
   Saturday afternoon through Saturday night.

   ...Synopsis...

   The remnants of Hurricane Isaias initially over southwest or
   west-central AL Saturday morning are forecast to advance
   north-northwest before turning north and then northeast through the
   TN Valley Saturday night. The system will be in the process of
   undergoing extratropical transition owing to its phasing with a
   subtropical branch trough, resulting in the broadening of an
   enhanced, southerly deep-layer wind field along and to the east of
   the cyclone track.

   Elsewhere, Tropical Storm Rachel will approach northern Baja and the
   lower-CO Valley late Saturday night/early Sunday morning as it is
   drawn into the southern extension of a strengthening midlevel trough
   along the West Coast.


   ...Southeast...

   As the primary surface low develops north into the TN Valley, it
   will become increasingly displaced from the effective warm sector,
   which is forecast to advance inland through GA and the Carolinas,
   along and south of a warm (or retreating wedge) front. Considerable
   cloud cover and areas of precipitation are expected to limit daytime
   heating within the poleward-expanding warm sector. However,
   dewpoints in the low-mid 70s will largely contribute to modest
   instability with MLCAPE approaching 1000 J/kg in some areas. Where
   sufficient destabilization can occur, the presence of a relatively
   strong deep-layer wind field with sizable SRH will support
   supercells capable tornadoes centered largely over southern and
   central GA Saturday with that threat spreading into parts of the
   Carolinas Saturday evening and night.

   A conditional intensity group 1 tornado contour was considered over
   portions of central GA where low-level shear is forecast to be
   maximized during the peak of the diurnal heating cycle. However,
   uncertainties in the degree of air mass destabilization precluded
   the inclusion of that contour, as well as any higher unconditional
   tornado probabilities.  


   ...Lower Colorado Valley...

   Deep-layer moisture is expected to increase through the forecast
   period within a zone of strengthening low/midlevel flow preceding
   the tropical system. The moisture increase will combine with daytime
   heating to yield pockets of moderate instability Saturday afternoon,
   supporting the potential for isolated strong to severe storms
   capable of severe wind gusts. A comparatively greater risk for
   severe wind gusts and perhaps a tornado or two is expected to
   materialize Saturday night into early Sunday as vertical shear and
   forcing for ascent strengthen across the region. 


   ...Great Basin...  

   A belt of 40-50 kt midlevel flow is forecast downstream from the
   evolving, western U.S. trough. Steepening low/midlevel lapse rates
   are expected to support modest instability by afternoon, which will
   coincide with sufficient deep-layer shear to support a few strong
   storms capable of gusty winds Saturday afternoon and evening. If
   subsequent model data indicate stronger instability, low severe
   weather probabilities may need to be included.

   ..Mead.. 10/09/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1730Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 090728

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0228 AM CDT Fri Oct 09 2026

   Valid 111200Z - 121200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS OVER PORTIONS OF
   THE CAROLINAS INTO THE DELMARVA AND ACROSS PARTS OF THE LOWER
   COLORADO VALLEY...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Isolated severe storms capable of damaging wind gusts and perhaps a
   few tornadoes appear possible over portions of the Carolinas into
   the Delmarva Sunday into Sunday evening, and parts of the lower
   Colorado Valley mainly Sunday morning.

   ...Synopsis...

   A mid/upper-level low over KY/TN Sunday morning is forecast to
   evolve into an open wave within a broader-scale trough progressing
   through the central and southern Appalachians toward the Atlantic
   Coast. Elsewhere, the remnants of Tropical Storm Rachel initially
   over southern CA will become increasingly sheared within a broad
   belt of enhanced midlevel flow extending from the Desert Southwest
   into the central Rockies. At the surface, an area of low pressure
   will develop from KY into the upper OH Valley with secondary
   cyclogenesis forecast on Sunday afternoon in the lee of the Blue
   Ridge over central VA. That cyclone will be collocated with a
   surface trough advancing east through the Piedmont and Coastal Plain
   and a warm front lifting north through the southern Mid-Atlantic.


   ...Delmarva into the Carolinas...

   Considerable strengthening of the deep-layer wind field is forecast
   on Sunday in advance of the midlevel trough. However, considerable
   cloud cover and areas of precipitation appear likely to limit air
   mass destabilization within the poleward-expanding warm sector.
   Nonetheless, boundary-layer dewpoints in the upper 60s to mid 70s
   will support pockets of modest instability, especially in areas
   where cloud breaks may occur. And given the presence of relatively
   strong low-level and deep-layer shear, a conditional risk for severe
   storms capable of damaging winds and perhaps a few tornadoes will
   exist Sunday into Sunday evening. Higher severe weather
   probabilities may be required in later forecasts if subsequent model
   data indicate greater instability than that currently depicted.


   ...Lower Colorado and Vicinity...

   As detailed in the recently issued Day 2 Convective Outlook, the
   enhancement of deep-layer shear and forcing for ascent will coincide
   with an at least modestly unstable air mass late Saturday night into
   early Sunday. That regime is likely to persist through at least
   Sunday morning with an associated risk for a few severe storms
   capable of severe wind gusts and perhaps a brief tornado or two. The
   overall weakening of the midlevel trough by afternoon and limited
   instability lead to uncertainty as to whether any severe weather
   threat will spread north into the Great Basin and central Rockies.

   ..Mead.. 10/09/2026

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 3 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1930Z

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
